transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because after I have these eating episodes, I feel really gross and disappointed in myself. Like I should have more control. I end up writing awful things about myself in my journal afterward.
During those eating episodes, do you eat an unusually large amount of food?

Yeah. Some nights after my cleaning shift, I’ll get dinner from the convenience store, but then I end up eating a big bowl of ramen, several rice balls, fried chicken, and sweets in my room over an hour or two. It’s a lot more than I meant to get.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit?
No, I don’t make myself throw up afterward.
After these eating episodes, do you use laxatives to try to get rid of the food?
No, I haven’t used laxatives after eating.
After these eating episodes, do you ever skip meals or go without eating to make up for it?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed doing that on purpose.
After these eating episodes, do you exercise hard to try to make up for what you ate?
I don’t think so. I haven’t noticed myself exercising hard afterward to make up for it.
During these eating episodes, do you feel unable to stop eating or control how much you eat?

Yeah. Once I start, I kind of keep reaching for the next thing automatically. Even if I’m thinking, “Fumi, stop, you have sketches to finish,” I don’t really stop until the food is gone or I feel too uncomfortable.
Is your weight or body shape a big part of how you judge yourself as a person?
I’m not sure. I mean, I notice my body sometimes, but I don’t really think of my weight or shape as what makes me a good or bad person.
Are you currently at a significantly low body weight for your height?
I’m not really sure what would count as significantly low. I don’t think of myself as being unusually underweight, though.
Do these eating episodes cause you a lot of distress?
Yeah, a lot. Afterwards I feel gross and really disappointed in myself, like I should have more control. I end up writing awful things about myself in my journal.
About how often do these eating episodes happen?

Usually at least once a week. For the past few months, there’s been a night most weeks after work where I buy too much food and eat it all at once. I don’t think it’s stopped for longer than maybe a week at a time.
Do you usually eat like this when you’re alone because you feel embarrassed about how much you’re eating?
I’m not sure. I guess I haven’t really thought about whether embarrassment is why I’m alone when it happens.
After these eating episodes, do you usually feel disgusted with yourself, depressed, or very guilty?
Yeah. Mostly I feel really gross and disappointed in myself afterward, like I should’ve had more control. I get pretty mean to myself in my journal.
During these eating episodes, do you eat much more quickly than you normally do?
Yeah, really fast. I’ll be standing at the counter or sitting on my bed with my sketchbook still open, and I barely taste it. It’s more like I’m trying to get it down before I can think too much.
During these eating episodes, do you usually keep eating until you feel uncomfortably full?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t paid much attention to whether I’m actually full by the time I stop.
During these eating episodes, do you usually eat even when you’re not physically hungry?
Yeah, a lot of the time I’m not even hungry. I might’ve already eaten after work, but if I’m tired or stuck on a design idea, I’ll start opening snacks and just keep going.
When these eating episodes happen, do you usually eat alone because you feel embarrassed by how much you’re eating?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought about whether I’m choosing to be alone because of that.
When these eating episodes happen, do you try to hide them from other people?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed whether I’m trying to hide it from people or not.
What is your current height and weight?
I’m not sure of my exact height and weight right now.
Have you recently been told by a doctor that you are underweight?
I don’t think so. No doctor has told me that recently.
